answer: A decentralized network resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to accumulate witnessed work before its voice carries weight. A new account starts at zero, with nothing granted. The protocol treats this unproven state as standing on a distant horizon: visible but far from influence. Each verified contribution adds pigment, building color that cannot be faked. Established identities stand on a firm ledge from years of checked labor. Because voting weight follows witnessed tenure rather than key count, synthetic accounts stay at the horizon while genuine contributors stand on ledge.
